title: One place, one job
header_line: My analysis of one book on habits. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Does your workspace do only one job?
A student described making a rule visible in his home so that others kept it in mind when making decisions, even though it was never needed. He said people knew it was there.

I said that we can set these things up around us all the time, and there are certain places where I know it is a good time for a small treat. I said I have to remove myself from that environment at times.

A student said: I have to completely separate the work environment from the house and life. The office is strictly for work and nothing else happens there. In an office with employees you eliminate distractions.

I said that I call them rituals: morning rituals. I get up early, read and do my to-do list, and keep that habit in any environment. As soon as I open my eyes that is my trigger to start being productive.
I said that I use the early hours to evaluate what I am doing wrong and could do better, and the next hours for communication and delegation.
What is the one room or hour that you keep for one job only?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the places you work and live in.
Write which job each place does.
Write what you will keep out of your work space.
Write what you will do in the early hours that you cannot do later.

check.q: What did a student say about the office?
What did I call my morning routine?
What is my trigger to start being productive?

recap: One place, one job. Keep your rituals wherever you are.
